semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For fixed positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r) = 1 and r <= d, there is a uniform nonnegative bound B such that every integer n greater than 1 and congruent to 1 modulo 2d admits a Laurent polynomial C_{d,r,n}(X,q) whose X exponents lie between -B and B and whose coefficients are integer Laurent polynomials in q. With this choice, the associated terms G_{d,r,n,k}(q) satisfy a telescoping relation H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = G_{d,r,n,k}(q) - G_{d,r,n,k+1}(q) for all k from 0 to n - 1, and the boundary values G_{d,r,n,0}(q) and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) can be written as M_n(q) times a polynomial divided by a polynomial coprime to M_n(q).

payload.statement_nl:
Let [m]_q = (1-q^m)/(1-q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-a q^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d. Then there exists a nonnegative integer B such that for every integer n > 1 satisfying n ≡ 1 mod 2d there exists a Laurent polynomial in X over Z[q^±1] of the form C_{d,r,n}(X,q) = ∑_{j=-B}^{B} c_j(q) X^j, with each c_j(q) in Z[q^±1], having the following property. Define the modulus M_n(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. For each integer k with 0 <= k <= n define
T_{d,r,n,k}(q) = [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k,
and define
G_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q) · C_{d,r,n}(q^k,q).
Also define
H_{d,r,n,0}(q) = [r]_q - [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2},
and for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1 define
H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q).
Then H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = G_{d,r,n,k}(q) - G_{d,r,n,k+1}(q) for every integer k with 0 <= k <= n-1, and there exist polynomials A_0(q), B_0(q), A_n(q), and B_n(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_0(q), M_n(q)) = 1, gcd(B_n(q), M_n(q)) = 1, G_{d,r,n,0}(q) = M_n(q) A_0(q) / B_0(q), and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) = M_n(q) A_n(q) / B_n(q).

detailed_findings.finding: No proof content was provided, so there is no construction of the claimed uniform bound B or the witness Laurent polynomials C_{d,r,n}(X,q).
The telescoping identity H_{d,r,n,k}=G_{d,r,n,k}-G_{d,r,n,k+1} and the endpoint divisibility/copimality conditions are substantial separate obligations, and none are verified.

The proposed counterexample is only an unsupported assertion; the specific choice n=2B+13 does not itself establish that a Laurent polynomial with support [-B,B] cannot satisfy the required identities.
No undeclared or forbidden citations were used.

result_payload.feedback_for_solver: Decompose this lemma into smaller pieces. At minimum: (1) derive the explicit ratio R_{d,r,n,k}(q)=T_{d,r,n,k+1}(q)/T_{d,r,n,k}(q); (2) rewrite the telescoping condition as a recurrence for C_{d,r,n}(q^k,q), including the special k=0 boundary term; (3) either provide an explicit closed-form Laurent polynomial C_{d,r,n}(X,q) with support bounded independently of n, or else weaken the lemma if such a uniform bound is not actually available; (4) prove the endpoint divisibility statements separately from the telescoping identity. If the intended path is disproof, give a fully explicit fixed instance (specific d,r,B,n) and show the resulting linear system for the coefficients c_j(q) is inconsistent, rather than only asserting this generically.
result_payload.reason: The submitted proof is empty, so none of the essential obligations are addressed: existence of a uniform bound B independent of n, construction of the Laurent polynomial C_{d,r,n}(X,q), verification of the telescoping identity for all k, and proof of the endpoint divisibility/copimality conditions. This is not a localized gap but an entirely missing argument for a strong theorem-specific certificate. The proposed counterexample is not yet certified: it asserts that for d=r=1 and n=2B+13 no bounded-support certificate exists, but no contradiction is derived, and that choice of n does not by itself force an interpolation impossibility. Thus the statement should be treated as suspect rather than false. No dependency violations are present.
